- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) and forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.0) and forecast is falling, increase forecast slope to avoid premature bearishness.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast decline by 10–20% in next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is flat (0.0) and price history shows mean reversion, model often fails to revert — adjust forecast to align with recent 7–14 day average.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >15% from 18-day moving average, apply a correction factor based on sentiment direction: +10% if sentiment >0.2, -10% if sentiment <0.2.  
- If forecast is flat (±0.5% over 5 days) and true outcome shows volatility, increase forecast variance by 5–10% to reflect sentiment-driven noise.
